ledger.note: 1443: Urbino becomes a duchy. 'The papal nomination transformed the county of Urbino, established in 1213, into a duchy governed by the House of Montefeltro'; the duke list begins '1443-1444: Oddantonio da Montefeltro (first)'. The land is my reading.
22 July 1444: Oddantonio is assassinated and Federico da Montefeltro seizes Urbino, 'recognized only as Count of Urbino'.
1474: Sixtus IV makes Federico Duke of Urbino. 'Sixtus IV gave him the title of Duke of Urbino in 1474'; the Duchy page says 'Confirmed duke in 1474'.

region.text: Pesaro e Urbino province with Gubbio

ledger.note: 1502: Cesare Borgia takes Urbino. 'After the short rule by Cesare Borgia in 1502-03, the dukedom went to the della Rovere papal family.' The page gives no month.

region.text: Pesaro e Urbino province with Gubbio

ledger.note: 1503: the Borgia rule ends (page: 'in 1502-03'); the dukedom passes to the Della Rovere in 1508 on Guidobaldo's death.
10 April 1508: Guidobaldo da Montefeltro dies without children after adopting his sister Giovanna's firstborn; Francesco Maria I della Rovere reigns 1508-1516 (table).

notes: Written from two pages. Unsettled: the extent in each reign (Fossombrone, Pesaro, Senigallia, Fano, Cesena, Bertinoro, Sassocorvaro, San Leo and Camerino are undated or absent on the pages; Federico's 1463 conquests were taken as vicar of the pope and are not drawn), the 1625 against 1631 date of the devolution, and the Medici interlude (1516-1521). The Papal States dossier (eu-13-d) wanted this state for 1631 only; the start year here is the page's 1443. Counterpart duchy-of-romagna (Cesare Borgia, 1500-1503) needs a dossier.
